course: The Mountain Course at Spruce Peak

facts.fact: The Mount Mansfield single chairlift at Stowe opened on 17 November 1940 and was billed as the longest and highest chairlift in the world (6,330 ft long, 2,030 ft vertical); it ran until 1986.
Spruce Peak opened for skiing in the 1949-50 season; the Spruce Peak base was redeveloped in the 2000s (new quads 2004-06, the Over Easy gondola 2006-07).

The Mountain Course at Spruce Peak (Stowe Mountain Club), a Bob Cupp design opened in 2007, lies at the base of Spruce Peak; its holes run through spruce-fir and northern hardwood forest (2023 Vermont lidar and orthophoto).
The chair's red and the spruce are a drawing choice for the ski-area setting (interpretation), not the club's colours.

concepts.name: The Single Chair
concepts.rationale: A vintage red single chairlift chair on its haul cable, with a dark red-spruce spire behind it: the ski mountain the course sits under, and the tree the peak is named for.
concepts.symbolism: the chair is Stowe's ski history (the 1940 single chair); the spruce is Spruce Peak
concepts.interpretation: the chair is a generic vintage single chair, not a drawing of a particular lift
concepts.strengths: reads at 32 px as a ski lift and a conifer; no other course uses either
concepts.tradeoffs: says ski resort more than golf, on purpose: the course is the resort's summer face
